title: Adversarial eviction throughput probe: tokenization-aware KV cache stress & p95 analysis
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Background: Recent customer incidents showed sporadic p95 token latency spikes correlated with high eviction churn in the KV/prefix cache under workloads that include long token sequences and variable tokenization boundaries. Existing harnesses measure hit-rate vs memory but do not exercise adversarial key sequences that intentionally align/misalign token boundaries to reveal worst-case eviction cost.

Goal: Build an adversarial eviction probe that is tokenization-aware and measures tokens/sec, per-token p95 latency, and hit-rate vs memory under controlled eviction pressure. The probe should capture interaction effects between key-length distributions, tokenization splits (subword boundaries), eviction policy (LRU vs CLOCK), and prefetch toggles. The harness must be regression-detection ready (baseline comparison, automated significance test, alerting thresholds).

Hypotheses: 1) Misaligned token boundaries amplify eviction overhead and increase p95 during prefix cache misses. 2) CLOCK with small shard sizes reduces tail latency vs strict LRU in bursty tokenized workloads. 3) Enabling lightweight prefetch reduces tokens/sec variance but may increase mean memory residency.

Success criteria (for this ticket):
- Deliver probe harness + CLI to run matrix sweeps and emit standardized CSV/JSON metrics.
- Produce a baseline sweep (current main at commit f4a2b1c) and a regression comparator that flags >10% increase in p95 or >15% drop in tokens/sec with p<0.05 (bootstrap test).
- Add Grafana dashboard panels and alert rule prototype for nightly regression detection.

Experiment matrix (dimensions):
- Cache memory budget: [128MB, 512MB, 2GB]
- Key-length distribution: [short(1-8 tokens), mixed(1-64), long(32-512)]
- Tokenization alignment: [aligned (tokens break at stable prefixes), misaligned (prefixes split across tokens), randomized subword splits]
- Eviction policy: [LRU, CLOCK, segmented-LRU]
- Prefetch: [disabled, lightweight, aggressive]
- Concurrency: [1, 8, 32 worker threads]
- Request pattern: [steady-state stream, microburst bursts (500ms bursts), adversarial churn (hotset rotate per 10k reqs)]

Metrics to capture: tokens_per_sec, per_token_p50/p95/p99, per-request latency, hit_rate, eviction_rate, memory_bytes, CPU%, GPU%, IO wait, kv_shard_contention_events. Raw traces for a sample of requests (1000) with prefix/cached key annotations to reproduce.

Implementation notes:
- Harness code path: tools/benchmarks/kv_eviction_probe (proto language: Go, follows existing harness patterns).
- Measurement: use high-resolution token timing at generator and apply correction for client-side jitter. Align token boundaries with the same tokenizer used by model runtime to avoid measurement artifacts.
- Regression detector: reference CSV baseline files under s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/kv-eviction/baselines/ and comparator tool that produces an HTML summary.
- Dashboard: grafana/dashboard/kv-eviction-adversarial.json (panel IDs created) and alert rule kv-eviction-regression-nightly.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Measurement noise from tokenization mismatch: mitigated by using the exact runtime tokenizer binary in the harness and repeating runs 10x with different random seeds.
- Large matrix runtime cost: run full matrix on dedicated nightly infra; use factorial sampling for PR-level quick checks.
- False positives from transient infra: require 3 consecutive nightly failures before paging on-call.

Deliverables:
- tools/benchmarks/kv_eviction_probe (CLI + config YAML templates)
- Baseline sweep CSVs and comparator tool
- Grafana dashboard + initial alert rules
- Confluence doc: Performance playbook section with reproducer steps

References & artifacts:
- Confluence doc (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/KEP-Adversarial+KV+Eviction+Probe
- Baseline bucket: s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/kv-eviction/baselines/
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/12987 (bench harness skeleton)
- Tokenizer binary used: docker.pkg.redwood.io/bench/tokenizer:v2026-03-01

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Finish harness core (config, runner, sample recorder) — assigned.
2) Wire up baseline sweep and store outputs to S3.
3) Create Grafana dashboard and one alert rule for nightly regression.
4) Run initial matrix and create an executive summary note for performance-review channel.
